takeaways: Aggressive AI-related capital expenditure is forcing a rotation into value stocks and prompting utilities to shift infrastructure costs onto tech giants, potentially compressing future free cash flows.

Central banks are increasingly utilizing gold as a neutral reserve anchor to hedge against geopolitical sanctions and currency volatility, even as Japan coordinates with the U.S. to stabilize bond markets.
China's slowing domestic demand and property sector weakness are fueling aggressive currency intervention and price wars in the EV market, signaling significant risks to regional economic stability.

items.title: Gold Erases Early Rally as WGC Reports First-Half Central Bank Buying at Lowest Since 2022
bullets: Central bank gold buying has slowed to its weakest first-half pace since 2022, with Russia and Turkey emerging as notable sellers to address budget deficits and currency support.
The recent coordinated currency intervention by Japan and the US, involving over $65 billion in total, has introduced significant volatility and prompted a reassessment of reserve asset strategies.
items.reason: Signals a shift in central bank reserve management and highlights major G7 currency intervention.

items.title: How M’East crisis narrows CBN’s options in fighting inflation
bullets: Persistent Middle East instability is forcing emerging market central banks into a 'higher-for-longer' interest rate stance to combat imported inflation and currency volatility.

The Central Bank of Nigeria is prioritizing structural reforms and increased oil production to reduce economic vulnerability, signaling that monetary policy alone is insufficient to manage current global shocks.
items.reason: Highlights the transmission of geopolitical risk to emerging market monetary policy.

items.title: Why Gold Is Emerging as the Reserve Asset of a Multipolar Global Economy
bullets: A stronger US dollar is paradoxically incentivizing central banks to diversify away from the greenback, as high debt-servicing costs and geopolitical sanctions risks drive demand for 'outside money'.
Reserve managers are increasingly viewing gold as a neutral anchor in a multipolar system, marking a long-term strategic shift rather than a temporary tactical adjustment to balance-sheet risks.
items.reason: Provides a structural analysis of long-term shifts in global reserve composition.

items.title: Here's the single biggest reason the bull market is broadening
bullets: Aggressive AI-related capital expenditure by tech giants like Meta and Alphabet is suppressing free cash flow, prompting investors to rotate capital into value-oriented sectors and small-cap stocks.
For the first time since 2009, the equally weighted S&P 500 has outperformed the market-cap-weighted index by over 7.3%, signaling a significant shift in market leadership and participation.
items.reason: Structural shift in market leadership

items.title: SpaceX's first-ever earnings report comes as stock hits new all-time low: Q2 preview
bullets: SpaceX faces a critical liquidity event on August 6 as a lockup expiration releases insider shares equivalent to triple the current tradable float, potentially exacerbating downward price pressure.

Analysts are concerned that massive projected capex, rising from $48.7 billion this year to $118.4 billion by 2028, may fail to generate adequate returns, mirroring broader investor skepticism regarding AI infrastructure spending.
items.reason: High-profile IPO volatility and liquidity risk

items.title: Why the U.S. stepped in after decades to prop up Japan's yen — and what's at stake
bullets: The U.S. participated in a rare joint intervention to support the yen primarily to prevent Japan from liquidating its massive holdings of U.S. Treasurys to fund unilateral market operations. Such a sell-off could have destabilized the dollar and exacerbated rising long-term borrowing costs in the U.S. market.

Japan plans to utilize the Federal Reserve's FIMA repo facility for future interventions, a strategic move intended to provide necessary dollar liquidity without forcing the sale of government debt. This mechanism serves as a critical signaling tool to stabilize global bond markets while addressing concerns over Japan's fiscal policy impact.
items.reason: Direct impact on U.S. Treasury market stability and global central bank coordination.

items.title: Global Market: Euro zone bond yields decline as falling oil prices boost market sentiment
bullets: German 10-year and 2-year bond yields fell by 5 basis points as lower crude oil prices reduced immediate inflation expectations. This shift in energy pricing has directly influenced money market pricing, with traders paring back expectations for additional European Central Bank rate hikes.

The correlation between energy prices and sovereign debt remains a primary driver for European fixed income, as investors monitor potential diplomatic progress in the Middle East. Sustained declines in oil prices are now viewed as a critical factor in easing the pressure on central banks to maintain aggressive monetary tightening.
items.reason: Highlights the sensitivity of global bond yields to energy-driven inflation and central bank policy shifts.

items.title: How likely is Beijing to walk the talk on boosting consumption?
bullets: China's Q2 GDP growth decelerated to 4.3% from 5% in the first quarter, highlighting the fragility of the economy as it struggles to meet the official 4.5-5% annual target.

Domestic demand is significantly underperforming, evidenced by a 5.7% decline in fixed-asset investment, an 18% plunge in property investment, and a sharp slowdown in retail sales growth to just 0.2%.
items.reason: Signals critical structural weakness in China's primary growth drivers.

items.title: The World Should Not Ignore China’s Undervalued Currency
bullets: China's current account surplus is estimated to be between 30% and 35% undervalued when accounting for misreported investment income and surging gold imports, suggesting significant currency manipulation.
The PBOC is actively intervening in foreign exchange markets, purchasing approximately $50 billion monthly to suppress the renminbi and maintain export competitiveness despite global trade tensions.
items.reason: Highlights potential for increased trade friction and currency volatility.

items.title: Hong Kong: Growth seen moderating – UOB
bullets: Hong Kong's GDP growth slowed to 4.3% year-on-year in 2Q26, with a 0.6% quarterly contraction marking the first such decline since 4Q22 and signaling a loss of economic momentum.

While the residential property market shows resilience with a 12.7% year-on-year price increase, analysts warn of downside risks from tighter Mainland capital controls and geopolitical uncertainties affecting future growth.
items.reason: Macroeconomic data indicating a potential slowdown in growth momentum.

items.title: Zhongji Innolight listing is largest Hong Kong IPO since 2019
bullets: Optical module leader Zhongji Innolight raised HKD53.41 billion in its dual listing, marking the largest IPO in Hong Kong since Alibaba in 2019 and highlighting continued demand for AI-related infrastructure plays.

The offering attracted significant institutional backing from 33 cornerstone investors, including major global firms like BlackRock, JP Morgan Asset Management, and Temasek, alongside key Chinese tech giants Alibaba and Tencent.
items.reason: Significant capital market activity signaling renewed interest in HKEX listings.

items.title: Australia ups demands on Big Tech firms to pay for news stories
bullets: The Australian government is introducing legislation to impose a 2.5% levy on the digital advertising revenue of major tech firms, such as Meta, Google, and TikTok, if they fail to secure commercial content deals with local news publishers.

While the levy rate is higher than the previously proposed 2.25%, the government has granted a key concession by limiting the tax base to digital advertising revenue rather than total corporate revenue, significantly reducing the potential financial impact.
items.reason: Regulatory shift impacting Big Tech revenue models in a major market.

items.title: Trump Says He Has Told Big Tech Companies to Build Their Own Power Plants
bullets: President Trump announced a new policy requiring major technology companies to construct their own power generation facilities to support data centers, aiming to mitigate rising electricity costs for residential consumers.

This policy shift addresses growing local opposition to energy-intensive AI infrastructure and signals potential capital expenditure increases for tech giants as they are forced to internalize the costs of their energy consumption.
items.reason: Significant policy intervention affecting AI infrastructure costs and utility sector dynamics.

items.title: Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmaps — breaking down TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and GlobalFoundries' approach to next-generation scale-up connectivity
bullets: As AI cluster bandwidth requirements exceed the physical limits of traditional electrical copper traces, the industry is shifting toward co-packaged optics (CPO) to integrate optical engines directly onto processor packages.

This transition is critical for reducing power consumption and latency in next-generation AI infrastructure, creating a massive new supply chain ecosystem involving foundries, OSATs, and specialized optical component manufacturers.
items.reason: Addresses a critical physical bottleneck for future AI hardware scaling.

items.title: US scrutinizing Anthropic's artificial intelligence training methods
bullets: Federal scrutiny of Anthropic's training methodologies signals a tightening regulatory environment for foundation model developers, potentially impacting the speed and cost of future model iterations.

Investors should monitor this development as a bellwether for increased oversight on data sourcing and model safety, which could force significant changes in the operational models of leading AI labs.
items.reason: Regulatory risk for major AI players impacts valuation and development timelines.

items.title: TSMC Approaching A New Milestone With Its 2nm Process By The End Of 2026 With 100,000 Monthly Wafers; NVIDIA, AMD, & Others Force Manufacturing Acceleration
bullets: TSMC is accelerating its 2nm production roadmap, targeting a capacity of 100,000 wafers per month by the end of 2026 to meet intense demand from major AI chip designers like Nvidia and AMD.

This rapid scaling of advanced node manufacturing underscores TSMC's dominant market position and its ability to maintain a technological lead over competitors struggling with yield and capacity constraints.
items.reason: Significant capacity expansion for critical AI infrastructure.

items.title: Goldman Sachs adds Applied Materials to the conviction buy list
bullets: Goldman Sachs has added Applied Materials to its conviction buy list, citing the company's superior positioning within the semiconductor ecosystem to capture sustainable, long-term demand.

The firm highlights that Applied Materials possesses an outsized growth runway compared to its peers, driven by its essential role in providing the equipment necessary for advanced chip manufacturing.
items.reason: Bullish analyst sentiment on a key semiconductor equipment supplier.

items.title: Price war fears grip China’s EV market after woeful July sales figures
bullets: Major premium EV manufacturers Xpeng, Nio, and Li Auto all reported month-on-month sales declines in July, signaling a potential cooling in demand for intelligent vehicles amid China's broader economic slowdown.

The synchronized downturn across these key players has heightened investor anxiety regarding a return to aggressive price-cutting strategies, which could severely compress profit margins across the Chinese EV sector.
items.reason: Signals potential margin compression and cooling demand in the world's largest EV market.

items.title: EVs and hybrids approach half of Australian new car sales amid ongoing fuel crisis
bullets: Battery electric vehicle sales in Australia more than doubled in Q2 2026 to 69,414 units, as consumers pivot away from internal combustion engines due to persistent fuel price volatility.

The market share for traditional petrol-powered vehicles dropped to a record low of 50.84%, indicating a rapid structural shift in consumer preference toward electrified powertrains in response to energy security concerns.
items.reason: Highlights a significant regional shift in consumer behavior driven by energy security and fuel costs.

items.title: Meta, Google Deals Aim to Protect Households From Data Center Power Costs
bullets: Utilities are increasingly mandating that tech giants like Meta and Google fully fund the infrastructure upgrades required for their AI data centers to prevent residential rate hikes.
A recent agreement between Entergy Louisiana and Meta is projected to generate $2 billion in customer savings over 20 years by shifting the full cost of service and grid expansion onto the developer.
items.reason: Highlights a critical shift in regulatory and utility cost-sharing models for AI infrastructure.

items.title: Empromptu AI Launches Grid Guard to Stop AI Data Centers From Breaking Their Own Power Infrastructure
bullets: Empromptu AI's new 'Grid Guard' software reduces power volatility in data centers by 80% by staggering GPU workloads, effectively smoothing out massive millisecond-level power spikes.

This technology addresses the industry's reliance on costly overbuilding of batteries and generators, offering a software-defined solution to optimize capital expenditure and improve grid stability for AI-scale facilities.
items.reason: Introduces a novel software-based efficiency solution for the high-cost problem of AI power volatility.

items.title: FAA proposal eyes fewer regulations for rocket launches, sparking concerns
bullets: The FAA has proposed a rule to waive key environmental and historic preservation regulations, including the National Environmental Policy Act and Clean Water Act, for commercial space licensing.

This regulatory shift could significantly accelerate launch cadences for companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin, though it faces strong opposition from environmental groups concerned about protected coastal habitats.
items.reason: Regulatory changes directly impact operational costs and timelines for major aerospace firms.

items.title: AI is ready to run spacecraft. Is the space industry ready for it?
bullets: With projections suggesting up to 70,000 new low-Earth orbit satellites in the next five years, human-led ground operations are becoming unsustainable for managing large-scale constellations.

Onboard AI processing is emerging as a critical investment area to enable autonomous data analysis and collision avoidance, which will significantly reduce operational overhead and latency for satellite operators.
items.reason: Highlights a critical technological shift necessary for the scalability of the multi-billion dollar satellite industry.
